sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: The load tests show we fall over at about twice our current traffic.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: {S3}, you had something on this?

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: That's well above what we expect at launch, though.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: True, but marketing is planning a big push.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Okay, we launch {PROJECT} on schedule and add autoscaling before the marketing push.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: {PROJECT}, okay.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Works for me.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Fine.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Do we really need to wait on the load test results?

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: We break at roughly double today's traffic, so there isn't much headroom.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Launch traffic should be way under that.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Fair enough, {S3}.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Unless the marketing push lands the same week.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Then the call is that {PROJECT} launches on time, and autoscaling goes in before marketing starts.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Ah, {PROJECT}, right.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Okay.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: We need to settle the database question today.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Option one is to stay on the current setup and add read replicas.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Option two is the managed service, which is cleaner but costs {MONEY} more per year.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Replicas only buy us maybe six months before we hit the same wall.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Let's go with the managed service, the extra cost is worth not redoing this in six months.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Agreed.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Honestly, read replicas would only buy us about six months.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: And to be fair, the managed service is {MONEY} more every year.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Still cheaper than doing this migration twice.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Agreed, we move to the managed service.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Okay, I'm convinced.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Last item, the offline mode.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: It's at least three weeks from done, and the release is on {DATE_ABS}.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Could we ship a partial version?

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Not really, half an offline mode is worse than none.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Then offline mode is out of this release, and we plan it for the next one.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Makes sense.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: A bit sad, but fine.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Offline mode, where are we?

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Three more weeks minimum, and we ship on {DATE_ABS}.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Then it moves to the next release, I don't want to rush it.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Can't we ship part of it?

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: A half-working offline mode would just generate tickets.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Fair, next release it is.
